issues.description: The problem statement first instructs that the SealSaloon has a final Stock stock that should be initialized in the constructor (instance field), but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static (shared across instances). This is an internal contradiction: a static field cannot be initialized per-instance in the constructor as described. The solution implements stock as a static final field, but the earlier instruction to initialize it in the constructor conflicts with the later requirement and the UML. Students may be confused whether stock should be an instance final field initialized in the constructor or a static shared field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: decide whether stock is an instance final field initialized in the constructor or a static shared field. If stock should be shared across all SealSaloon instances, update the earlier instruction to remove the requirement to initialize it in the constructor and state that it should be declared static final and initialized at declaration (as in the solution). If stock should be per-instance, remove the requirement that it must be static and adjust the solution/template accordingly.

issues.description: The problem specification (UML and descriptions) defines checkOrderReady() as a no-argument method (checkOrderReady(): void) and describes calling checkOrderReady() without parameters. The solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) which requires a parameter. This method-parameter mismatch means students implementing the no-arg version as specified would not match the solution's signature and tests (or vice versa), causing confusion on the expected signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature between specification, template, and solution. Preferably revert the solution to the no-argument signature checkOrderReady() and handle any internal logging via a private flag or internal logic, or update the problem statement and UML to explicitly allow a boolean parameter and update the textual description to show the method takes a parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This introduces a naming/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (checking and serving ready orders) and can confuse students implementing the method according to the exercise specification. Students will expect to implement or call checkOrderReady() with no parameters as described in the problem, while the reference solution requires a boolean parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by providing a no-argument public method checkOrderReady() that performs the order-serving logic. If internal logging control is desired, implement a private helper checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and have the public no-arg checkOrderReady() call it (e.g., checkOrderReady(false)), preserving the UML/API expected signature.
